title: Completed maximal localizations are complete local flat tests for zero derived objects
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and work in its ordinary module derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset R$, put $R_{\mathfrak m}=(R\setminus\mathfrak m)^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and
$$B_{\mathfrak m}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1} R_{\mathfrak m}/(\mathfrak mR_{\mathfrak m})^n,$$
the maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] of $R_{\mathfrak m}$. Then $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR_{\mathfrak m}$; $B_{\mathfrak m}$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $(\mathfrak mR_{\mathfrak m})B_{\mathfrak m}$, complete for that ideal. The canonical map $R_{\mathfrak m}\to B_{\mathfrak m}$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and both $R\to R_{\mathfrak m}$ and $R\to B_{\mathfrak m}$ are flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Using derived extension of scalars [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], for every $K\in D(R)$ one has
$$K=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_{\mathfrak m}=0\text{ for every maximal ideal }\mathfrak m\subset R.$$
No boundedness or finite-generation assumption on $K$ is imposed; the assertion includes the zero ring, for which there are no maximal ideals.

source.place: Agent derived-category corollary of Tag 00MC, lemma-completion-faithfully-flat, and Tag 00HN, lemma-characterize-zero-local, parts (2) and (6), with the Noetherian local completion properties. proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and write $A=R_{\mathfrak m}$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mA$. A maximal ideal is prime: if $ab\in\mathfrak m$ and $a\notin\mathfrak m$, write $1=u+ra$ with $u\in\mathfrak m$ and deduce $b\in\mathfrak m$. Thus [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] identifies $A$ as a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. The complement of $\mathfrak m$ is multiplicative. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] to this localization: $A$ is Noetherian and $R\to A$ is flat. Since $\mathfrak n$ is a proper maximal ideal, $A/\mathfrak n$ is a nonzero field.

Put $B=\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak n^n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $B$ is Noetherian. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated, so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] says $B$ is $\mathfrak nB$-adically complete. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $B$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak nB$ and $B/\mathfrak nB\cong A/\mathfrak n$. This last ring is nonzero, hence $B$ is nonzero. These statements give all the requested completion properties, with exactly the extended maximal ideal appearing in the item.

The ring $A$ is Noetherian and local, so [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] gives faithful flatness of the canonical $A\to B$, and in particular flatness. Applying [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] to the flat $R$-algebra $A$ and the flat $A$-module $B$ proves that $R\to B$ is flat. This does not assert that $R\to B$ is faithfully flat for one chosen maximal ideal.

For any flat $R$-algebra $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] makes $F_S=(-)\otimes_R S$ an exact additive functor on modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] its termwise functor descends to derived categories; by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] this descent is also its total left derived functor. The extension of scalars specified by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is that left derived functor (ordinary modules are sheaves on the one-object site with only the maximal covering sieve), so it is computed termwise on any representative complex $C$ of $K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to $F_S$ to obtain $H^q(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S)\cong H^q(K)\otimes_R S$ for every integer $q$. No boundedness enters either cited exact-functor result.

proof.text: If $K=0$, its derived scalar extensions are zero: the derived extension functor is additive by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], hence carries a zero object to a zero object. Conversely assume all the displayed extensions are zero, and fix $q$. Put $M=H^q(K)$. Step 4 with $S=B$ gives $M\otimes_R B=0$ for each maximal ideal. Put $N=M\otimes_R A$. There is an isomorphism $N\otimes_A B\cong M\otimes_R B$, given by $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$, with inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$; the balancing relations verify both composites on pure tensors. Commute the two factors over $A$ and apply [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero] to the faithfully flat $A$-module $B$ from step 3. It follows that $M\otimes_R A=0$ for every maximal ideal.

source.place: Tags 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat) and 00HP (lemma-ff), followed by the elementary tensor balancing identifications.

proof.text: Write $S=R\setminus\mathfrak m$. Identify $M\otimes_R S^{-1}R$ with $S^{-1}M$ by $x\otimes(r/s)\mapsto rx/s$, inverse $x/s\mapsto x\otimes(1/s)$. The fraction relation and tensor balancing verify these inverse maps: a relation $t(s\prime x-sy)=0$ becomes zero after multiplication by the unit $tss\prime$, and the two composites send a fraction or pure tensor to itself. Thus step 5 gives $M_{\mathfrak m}=0$ for every maximal ideal. If $0\ne x\in M$, its annihilator $I=\{r\in R:rx=0\}$ is proper, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] supplies a maximal $\mathfrak m$ containing $I$. But $x/1=0$ in $M_{\mathfrak m}$ implies $sx=0$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak m$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], contradicting $s\in I$. Hence $M=0$. This is the elementwise argument of Tag 00HN(1)--(2), with no finite-generation hypothesis on $M$.

Step 6 holds for every $q$, so all $H^q(K)$ vanish. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], a representative $C$ then has the quasi-isomorphism $0\to C$, which becomes an isomorphism after localization; thus $K=0$. The reverse implication on cohomology also follows because each $H^q$ is a functor factoring through this localization. If $R=0$, every unital $R$-module is zero since $x=1x=0x=0$; consequently every complex and derived object is zero. There are no proper maximal ideals, so the right-hand condition is vacuous and the equivalence still holds.
